results.summary_before: This project is a simple VGA GPU that uses an ALU pipeline to compute pixel colors based on the pixel's x/y coordinates and a few configurable registers. The design takes pixel coordinates as input and outputs a color, with parameters set via registers. The documentation is very sparse, with testing instructions only suggesting to read the Verilog code, indicating limited support for users.
results.summary: This project generates a mesmerizing VGA display of hypnotic concentric rings that expand or contract from the center of the screen. It is designed as a demoscene-style visual effect for the Tiny Tapeout platform. The design takes speed and direction inputs and outputs RGB222 VGA signals with VSync and HSync. Testing requires connecting a Tiny VGA PMOD and a VGA monitor, then applying power and releasing reset.

results.summary_before: This circuit is a game that uses a single input switch to control gameplay. The input is debounced and edge-triggered, with rising and falling edges converted to pulses. The game is designed to work better with a switch rather than a button. No silicon test report is provided, so its hardware behavior is not confirmed.
results.summary: This circuit is a padlock that lets you set a code for a safe using pins 2 to 4 and pin 7. Pin 1 resets the safe, and the clock button is used to enter the code. The seven-segment display shows "L" for locked when pin 1 is on and the clock button is pressed. A partial silicon test report notes errors where the saved code inverts each clock cycle and the third code bit is ignored, so some invalid codes are accepted.

results.summary_before: This design is a simple event accumulator that counts rising edges on an input pin and outputs a 4-bit activity value. It includes a clock and active-low reset, and can be tested in simulation by driving the input with pulses and observing the outputs. The design is minimal and intended to illustrate basic stream processing without complex control logic. The documentation is sparse but sufficient to understand the basic functionality.
results.summary: This design connects inputs 0 and 1 to an AND gate whose output drives outputs 0, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Inputs 2 and 3 feed a second AND gate whose output drives output 4. Setting only the first two inputs to 1 should display the number five, while setting only inputs 2 and 3 lights the lower left segment. The documentation is sparse but sufficient to understand the basic functionality.
